transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I keep misplacing order tickets and other important things at the shop, and it’s starting to hurt my business. I recently took over running my own dry-cleaning boutique, and constantly losing these items is becoming really frustrating and causing some big mix-ups.
Have you noticed any other problems with your memory or concentration outside of work, such as forgetting appointments or where you placed your personal belongings?

Yes, absolutely, it's happening outside of work too. I'm constantly misplacing my personal keys and having to tear through my purse and the whole house looking for them. It's also straining my marriage because I zone out when my husband is talking, and I've been struggling to keep up with my church commitments.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, anxious, or irritable, alongside these memory and concentration issues?
I do feel quite stressed and frustrated about all the problems at the shop lately. But as for my overall mood, I haven't really noticed any major changes like deep sadness or anxiety.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'zoning out' when your husband is talking, is it that you're not paying attention or that you're actually having trouble following the conversation?

It’s like the words just go past me. Halfway through a conversation with my husband or my staff at the shop, I’ll suddenly realize I’ve zoned out and have to ask them to repeat themselves because I didn't register any of the details.

Do you find it difficult to focus on tasks that require sustained mental effort, such as reading a book or following a complex instruction, and if so, has this been a persistent issue or something that's developed recently?

Yes, if I try to focus on our booking software or even fold a big batch of shirts, my mind just drifts off after a few minutes and I catch myself staring at the wall. While this has become a major crisis since taking over the shop two years ago, it's actually a lifelong issue for me. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was easily distracted and constantly losing my worksheets.
Can you describe how your symptoms of distractibility and losing things have changed over time, and have you noticed any periods where these symptoms significantly improved or worsened?

I've had milder versions of these issues my whole life, dating back to elementary school where I would constantly lose worksheets and get distracted. They got significantly worse two years ago when I transitioned from being an employee to running my own boutique. Losing that structured environment and suddenly having to manage all the scheduling, bookkeeping, and inventory myself really made these difficulties stand out.

You mentioned that your symptoms of distractibility and losing things have been present since childhood but worsened significantly when you took over the boutique, can you tell me more about how these symptoms affected your academic and professional life before this significant change?

In elementary school, teachers always wrote on my report cards that I was constantly chatting, getting out of my seat, and losing my homework. Later, when I worked as an employee at a neighborhood dry cleaner, the highly structured routine helped mask my difficulties. Milder versions of my attention and organization issues were always there in the background, but the set structure kept me on track.
Have you ever experienced symptoms of restlessness, fidgeting, or an inability to engage in activities quietly, either as a child or in your current life?

Yes, I definitely feel restless and fidgety, and that's been true both now and as a child. Nowadays, I struggle to sit still during long church meetings or when doing computer work at the shop, constantly popping up to check on things or straighten racks. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was always getting out of my seat during class.

Can you tell me more about how your restlessness and fidgeting behaviors have impacted your daily life and relationships, and have you noticed any situations where these symptoms are particularly pronounced?

It's especially bad when I'm waiting in lines at the bank or the supply store, where I get so fidgety and impatient that I fight the urge to just walk out. This constant restlessness leaves me completely drained, and my husband complains that I'm just not present for him at home or at church anymore.
